paper_metadata.title: Enhanced mechanical properties of high-temperature-resistant Al-Cu cast alloy by microalloying with Mg

evidence.quote: The effects of microalloying with Mg (0 e0.23 wt%) on the microstructural evolution and mechanical properties of Al eCu 224 cast alloys at ambient and elevated temperatures are investigated
Tensile test bars were cast in a Stahl mold (ASTM B-108) at Arvida Research and Development Centre of Rio Tinto Aluminum, Quebec.

microalloying with Mg significantly enhances the precipitation of the q0 phase during aging, producing fine, dense, and uniformly distributed q0 precipitates.
These precipitates are much more effective for alloy strengthening than are the q00 precipitates in the alloy without Mg.
The as-cast microstructure (Fig. 1b) comprises the a-Al matrix, plate-like Al3(ZrVTi) particles, and the Al7Cu2Fe, Al2Cu, and Mg2Si eutectic phases.

No apparent difference among the microstructures of the as-cast experimental alloys was observed, except that the Mg2Si particles formed only at a higher Mg content (0.19%).
The average secondary dendrite arm spacing in the central region of the as-received bars was measured to be ~20 mm for all the experimental alloys
The average grain size of all the investigated alloys was found to be ~1 70 mm, indicating that Mg addition had no apparent effect on the grain structure and size of the alloys.
